question.text: A higher strike price for a call option (all else equal) results in:

explanation.text: The Logic: All else equal, a higher strike price lowers a call's intrinsic value and therefore reduces its premium. For puts, the reverse holds: a higher strike raises the put premium. The Trap: The directional relationship between strike and premium is opposite for calls and puts; do not assume strike moves both premiums the same way. Note: Pages 71-72 of the NISM Series-I workbook tie the call-price decrease specifically to lower intrinsic value when strike rises, and similarly support the higher put premium for a higher strike.
